Region Syddanmark is one of the five administrative regions of Denmark and a key participant in the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD). It plays a central role in both regional and national quality development for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) by contributing patient data and clinical experts to the database's steering committee. 

Between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023, the region registered a total of 7,181 IBD patients [^src1]. The diagnostic breakdown of this cohort showed that 41% of the region's IBD patients had [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]], 59% had [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]], and 41 patients were diagnosed with [[dk830f-primaer-skleroserende-kolangitis|DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]] [^src1].

In terms of clinical quality indicators, Region Syddanmark has demonstrated leading performance. Regarding [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], which tracks patient education for newly diagnosed individuals, all departments in Region Syddanmark successfully registered their educational activities. In contrast, 16 departments across the other four regions ([[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]]) had not yet begun registering this data [^src3]. Furthermore, for [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], Region Syddanmark was the only region to meet the development goal, ensuring that all patients received their recommended follow-up on time [^src3].

The region also actively engages with the database's findings to drive local improvements. In its formal response to the [[danibd-aarsrapport-2024]], Region Syddanmark highlighted an internal audit conducted at the OUH Odense Kirurgisk Afdeling A. Based on the audit's results, the department implemented targeted initiatives, including an increased focus on steroid tapering and improved dialogue with collaborators concerning acute patients [^src5].
